facts.text: Among the three pre-training tasks (SR, NSG, MDG), SR performs slightly better than the other two.
facts.source_quote: Among all three pre-training tasks, SR works slightly better than the other two tasks (i.e., NSG and MDG).

facts.text: The authors also tried randomly combining all three tasks during training, each used with 1/3 probability, denoted 'ALL'.
facts.source_quote: We also tried to randomly use all the three tasks during training with 1/3 probability each (indicated as ALL).

facts.text: When using only the unlabeled documents from the training splits of CNNDM or NYT (a limited amount of pre-training data), ALL generally outperforms each of the three individual tasks, possibly because of the limited number of unlabeled documents available in those training splits.
facts.source_quote: we observed that, in general, All outperforms all three tasks when employing unlabeled documents of training splits of CNNDM or NYT, which might be due to limited number of unlabeled documents of the training splits.

facts.text: After adding more pre-training data (the GIGA-CM dataset), SR consistently achieves the highest ROUGE-2 score on both CNNDM and NYT.
facts.source_quote: After adding more data (i.e., GIAG-CM) to pre-training, SR consistently achieves highest ROUGE-2 on both CNNDM and NYT.

facts.text: The authors conclude that SR is the most effective pre-training task, because sentence reordering requires comprehensively understanding a document at a wide scope beyond individual words and sentences, which closely matches the essence of abstractive document summarization.
facts.source_quote: We conclude that SR is the most effective task for pre-training since sentence reordering task requires comprehensively understanding a document in a wide coverage, going beyond individual words and sentences, which is highly close to the essense of abstractive document summarization.

relations.text: ALL only outperforms the individual tasks in the limited-data setting (unlabeled documents from the training splits alone); once more pre-training data is added, SR instead becomes the consistent top performer — so the claim 'SR is best' is scoped to the larger-data, primary setting rather than the small-data setting.
relations.source_quote: After adding more data (i.e., GIAG-CM) to pre-training, SR consistently achieves highest ROUGE-2 on both CNNDM and NYT.

relations.text: The authors' conclusion that SR is the most effective pre-training task follows from the observed outcome that SR consistently achieves the highest ROUGE-2 once more pre-training data is added.
relations.source_quote: We conclude that SR is the most effective task for pre-training
